problem: The security-acknowledgement gate cannot fire in production: the only minter of the confirm token passes securityAcknowledged unconditionally.
impact: consumeConfirmToken refuses a needs-approval proposal unless the token says a human acknowledged the findings, and its error text promises exactly that. The sole production caller hardcoded the literal, so a proposal whose evidence tripped the security scan was accepted through the ordinary two-step flow with the reviewer never shown, and never asked about, the finding. Pre-0.2.74 the same call had no flag and needs-approval could not be accepted by any route: the release replaced a visible dead end with a silent bypass, which is worse because the refusal used to be observable.
suggested_fix: Read the gate, print what the scan found and in which evidence, and require an explicit --acknowledge-security. A clean proposal claims no acknowledgement; an unreadable proposal refuses rather than assuming a pass.
evidence: Traced the full call chain; the only production call site is src/commands/workspace.ts:143, every other is a test. Found independently by two reviewers approaching from SAC and from the CLI.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Every production call site of mintConfirmToken enumerated with keryx ctx rg across src, excluding tests.

disposition.evidence: Fixed in #427 (bc4e193f): confirm-review reads the gate, prints the findings, and requires --acknowledge-security; the stored token is asserted, not the printed line.

verification.evidence: Re-checked at bc4e193f: restoring the exact shipped line turns the named test red 3/3 in isolation, and the test reads the persisted token rather than stdout. The bypass no longer reproduces.

problem: Session-history redaction covered message content but not tool-call arguments, so secrets reached disk in three files.
impact: redactHistory rewrote content and let the object spread carry toolCalls through untouched, while writeJsonl serialises them verbatim into context.jsonl, archive.jsonl and the legacy transcript.jsonl. A credential the model read from one tool result and passed into the next call's arguments was written unmasked — through the function whose own comment says a command that reads a credential must not leak the raw value.
suggested_fix: Redact arguments as text rather than parsing the JSON, since arguments are kept byte-exact as the provider emitted them and masks are fixed-width.
evidence: Read the type, the spread and the serialisation path; redactHistory was introduced in 508f7b2d and has no test coverage anywhere.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Traced every field writeJsonl serialises against every field redactHistory rewrites.

disposition.evidence: Fixed in #427 (bc4e193f); the test asserts all three files, including the legacy mirror.

verification.evidence: Re-checked at bc4e193f: restoring the shipped redactHistory turns the named test red 3/3. The secret no longer appears in any of the three files.

problem: A contract registered this release declares maxItems, which the validator has no branch for — the third instance of a declared-but-ignored keyword.
impact: review-pr-feedback-output says excluded_for_injection maxItems 0 when screen_status is unavailable — the machine form of 'if the injection screen never ran you may not claim it excluded anything'. A record asserting both validated clean at the enforcement point its own doc-comment names. minItems and maximum were the first two instances, each fixed by hand.
suggested_fix: Fix the class, not the instance: a guard that no shipped schema may declare a keyword validateValue ignores, with the implemented set derived from the validator source rather than hand-listed.
evidence: keryx skills contracts validate reported a self-contradictory record as valid; zero matches for maxItems in the validator.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Structural guard walks every schema in CONTRACTS and compares declared keywords against those the validator source reads.

disposition.evidence: Fixed in #427 (bc4e193f): maxItems implemented plus a structural guard, which immediately found exclusiveMinimum and `not` ignored in the contracts agents exchange.

verification.evidence: Re-checked at bc4e193f: deleting the maxItems branch turns the guard red (2 fail), and deleting exclusiveMinimum or `not` each turn it red as well. The self-contradictory record is now refused.

problem: The routable-target guard was wired into one of two write paths, and the unguarded one is the path agents are told to use.
impact: isRoutableSkillTarget was added after two prose-target skills reached main — matching no skills route query and verifying as permanently stale. createProjectSkill, which backs keryx skills create, never called it, and reviewer-skill-creator instructs agents to run exactly that command.
suggested_fix: Check the target before anything is inferred or written, so a rejection cannot leave a slug derived from prose.
evidence: Reviewer demonstrated with --dry-run that a full sentence was accepted as a target.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Both write paths enumerated: the SAC wrap-up writer and the CLI create command.

disposition.evidence: Fixed in #427 (bc4e193f); legitimate concept, symbol and path targets still pass.

verification.evidence: Re-checked at bc4e193f: removing the guard turns the named test red 3/3, and the three legitimate target shapes still pass, so the guard was not made over-broad.

problem: renderRiskHints reported '- none' for an output shape that carried a file count but no per-file rows.
impact: The count proves files changed and the empty row set proves none were inspected, yet the section said no risky files. Live: Changed files 2, Risk Hints none, with package.json among the two and matching the risk regex. Same false-clean class as the Changed files 0 fix this release made, one section further down — and the comment above it warned the class could recur there.
suggested_fix: Distinguish examined-and-clean from counted-but-unexamined; keep '- none' for a genuinely empty diff so the section stays useful.
evidence: Reproduced live against the real repo range, then confirmed the fix from source.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Both no-hint branches examined against all three shapes: empty diff, counted-but-unlisted, and listed-but-not-risky.

verification.evidence: Re-checked at bc4e193f: the exact reported invocation now reports unknown with the file count and the re-run advice; an empty diff still reports none; restoring the shipped branch turns the tests red 3/3.

problem: The regex-escaping expression in metadataLine escaped nothing: its character class closed at the first bracket.
impact: The class ended early, so the pattern became one metacharacter followed by two backslashes and a bracket, matching essentially nothing. Latent today because all three labels are metacharacter-free — but the next label added is the one that breaks it, and the failure would be a silently mis-extracted provenance field rather than an error.
suggested_fix: Fix the class and lift it to an exported helper, since through the public surface a fixed and a broken version are indistinguishable.
evidence: Ran the shipped expression against the intended one side by side; the shipped one is a no-op on a probe string of every metacharacter.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Single expression; all three call-site labels checked.

disposition.evidence: Fixed in #427 (bc4e193f) and exported as escapeRegexLiteral so it can be tested at all.

verification.evidence: Re-checked at bc4e193f: restoring the shipped character class turns the named test red 3/3, and the three real labels still pass through unchanged, so today's behaviour is unaltered.

problem: Four gates the release added could be deleted with the full suite green, and deleting both SAC truncation gates made the suite hang rather than fail.
impact: A hanging suite is worse than a failing one: CI reports a timeout, which reads as infrastructure trouble rather than a defect. The four unwatched gates were parseCheckpoint's key-set/version check, the tailOffset bounds check, and the blocked-note refusal in both the harness tool and the CLI — a guard duplicated across write paths with only one copy covered.
suggested_fix: Pin each gate with a test that fails when it is removed, and bound the read loop by a computed chunk count so removal can only produce a wrong digest, never a hang.
evidence: Mutation sweep over all fourteen gates, escalating each survivor to the full suite so under-targeting could not produce a false 'unguarded'.

class_scope.enumeration_method: All fourteen gates the release added were mutated; survivors escalated to the full suite.

disposition.evidence: Fixed in #428 (10741e10): four gates pinned, loop bounded.

verification.evidence: Re-checked at 10741e10: each of the four turns its named test red 3/3 when removed, and the double mutation that used to hang now completes.

problem: Two SAC truncation lines remain individually removable with the suite green.
impact: They are genuinely redundant — each refuses a truncated ledger alone, and a third check now backs both — so no test can discriminate them: same refusal for the same input. Reporting this as fixed would be a claim wider than the evidence, which is the class this programme exists to remove.
suggested_fix: State it rather than write a test that only appears to discriminate, and remove the hang risk separately by bounding the loop.
evidence: Removing either alone leaves 30 tests green; removing both used to hang and now completes.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Both lines mutated individually and together.

disposition.evidence: human: altsay — the operator asked to close everything closable; this pair is not closable by a test without fabricating a distinction that does not exist. Named in PR #428 and carried openly rather than silently.

verification.evidence: Confirmed as a real and accurate description of the remaining state: both lines still delete cleanly, and the hang no longer occurs.

problem: Three tests written during this flow initially passed for the wrong reason, and one added guard produced a false positive.
impact: One asserted printed output instead of the stored token, so restoring the shipped bug left it green; one sealed a checkpoint hash over the key it was testing, so the record failed its hash check instead of the gate; one omitted the session, so the command exited 1 with and without the guard. Separately, the new contract-keyword guard reported $ref as unimplemented because its scrape pattern missed a leading dollar. A guard that cries wolf earns an allow-list entry and is then deleted, so a false positive is the same class of error as a miss.
suggested_fix: Run the mutation before believing the test, and add a control to any test whose failure could have more than one cause.
evidence: All four caught by mutation rather than by reading, and corrected before landing.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Every test added by this flow was mutation-checked before the branch was pushed.

disposition.evidence: All three tests corrected and re-proved 3/3 before landing: the token test in bc4e193f, the checkpoint-hash and session-control tests in 10741e10. The contract-keyword guard's $ref false positive was fixed in bc4e193f before the branch was pushed.

verification.evidence: Re-checked at bc4e193f and 10741e10: each of the three corrected tests now turns red on the exact shipped line 3/3 in isolation, and the guard no longer reports $ref as unimplemented.

problem: The release also fixes three older leaks, which the checked-and-cleared lists recorded rather than missed.
impact: Memory, wiki and wiki-enrichment previously computed a guard decision and then wrote the ORIGINAL unredacted content to disk; wiki enrichment had no guard at all, so model-generated content reached disk unchecked. All three are genuinely fixed in this release. Recording them matters: a review that reports only defects gives a one-sided picture of a release that closed three real holes and opened two.
evidence: Reviewer verified each against the v0.2.73 source rather than assuming.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Each compared against its v0.2.73 source.

disposition.evidence: Not a defect: these are fixes, recorded so the release's balance is stated honestly rather than as findings-only.

verification.evidence: Confirmed against v0.2.73 that each of the three previously wrote unredacted content and now writes the redacted form.
